# No. 2 Arcade module contract, version 1

Phase 1 registers 24 notebook modules. Only `scribble-defender` is playable.
The remaining 23 modules intentionally return a still-blank page, not simulated
or partly implemented versions of their future games.

| Field / method | Contract |
|---|---|
| id, title, version | Stable save ID, configurable display title, implementation version. Defender remains 0.3.2 inside shell 0.4.0. |
| paperAsset, coverAsset, thumbAsset, titleAsset | Manifest IDs. Full cover and paper are decoded on opening; cover thumbnails belong to the lightweight hub. |
| init(seed, services) | Seeded state creation. Simulation has no document, window, renderer or storage dependency. |
| fixedStep | Exactly 1/120 second. |
| update(state, input, dt) | Fixed-step update. Render never consumes gameplay randomness. |
| drawList(state, services) | Shared registered sprite/text commands. Existing Defender uses its unchanged ScribbleScene. |
| input.map, input.rebindable | Action bindings; settings belong to this notebook. Defender's existing rebinding remains available. |
| scoring, highScoreTableId, highScores(save) | Three-character initials, descending top ten, stable namespaced table. |
| cheatSheet, perGameSettings | Student-written notes and game-local preferences. |
| attract(state) | Normal game input for a seeded demo. Blank modules return no input. |
| tests(services) | Deterministic suite. Defender calls all 34 original rule checks; blank modules identify themselves as blank. |
| mount / suspend / resume / destroy | Adapter lifecycle. Close stops simulation/audio, destroys owned textures and WebGL context, removes the frame and clears references. |

## Preservation boundary

`games/defender/baseline.html` is an exact SHA-256-checked v0.3.2 release.
The ten original source files beside it are byte-for-byte snapshots. The old
source project and every distributed release remain unchanged.

The Defender adapter is a compatibility module, not a rewritten simulation.
It mounts the existing UI in a same-origin srcdoc frame, using the shell's
single pinned PixiJS 8.6.6 library. The notebook owns a renderer instance and
WebGL context while open. This deliberate isolation preserves its DOM IDs,
input behavior, raster art, shared draw list and 120 Hz rules. Future modules
can use the shared renderer/asset services directly without the legacy DOM.

Composition injects only storage/input/audio service bridges, shared Pixi
ownership and a typographic-dash normalization required by this release.
The engine, CONFIG, scene and asset bytes are not edited. A passive event
observer records death tallies/achievements without changing RNG or state.
The original __SCRIBBLE_TEST__ callback is forwarded and the active
__SCRIBBLE_API__ remains available at the shell window.

The sharpener opens arcade settings and links to Defender's original settings
note. Its existing in-game note remains present so v0.3.2 art and UI are not
silently redrawn. Notebook page navigation suspends play; returning resumes
only if the player was not already paused. LB/L1 plus the D-pad focuses shell
page tabs. Selecting play hands normal controller input back to the notebook.

## Shared services and memory

The shell owns guarded persistence, global input/focus, the master audio bus,
paper/ink asset loading, geometry, layout verification and the pinned Pixi
library. The same No2Scene draw list positions real hub objects and their DOM
hit regions, and is consumed by offline raster QA. Raster source images keep
their aspect ratios. Only wood is cover-cropped to extend the table.

The desk is capped at seven game IDs plus one replay sketchbook. The backpack is a paginated stack of eight. Score progression is on by default, and a previous-game target of 10,000 is defined in catalog.progression. Only available builds can unlock. Locked covers remain visible in the backpack, cannot be pinned or opened, and explain that they are still being drawn. The optional override affects ready games only.

| Budget | Limit |
|---|---:|
| Standalone HTML, complete suite | 64 MiB |
| Hub and cover-thumbnail decoded source pixels | 32 MiB |
| An active blank notebook's cover, paper and shared ink | 12 MiB |
| Future simple game's atlases | 32 MiB |
| Future dense game's atlases | 64 MiB |
| Defender's unchanged atlas budget | 128 MiB; actual 74.1875 MiB |

Source pixel accounting is width x height x 4. It is not a GPU-driver RAM
measurement. Render targets, original Defender physical materials, browser
font/image caches and compositor buffers are reported separately or stated
as unmeasured. The old atlas budget never claimed to include these buffers.
No other game's gameplay textures are decoded when Defender opens. The
compressed Defender pack is decoded only on entering its play page. Closing
the notebook destroys its owned texture sources and context, not just its
visibility. Build sizes and lifecycle evidence live in build/sizes.json and QA.

## Save expansion, migration and rollback

Keys use `No2Arcade:game:<stable-id>:settings`, `scores`, `best`, and `stats`.
Arcade preferences, progress, desk layout and the migration marker have
separate No2Arcade keys. All storage reads and writes have guarded fallbacks.

The original keys scribble-settings-v2, scribble-scores-v2 and
scribble-defender-high are copied without deleting or rewriting them. An
idempotent marker is written only after successful persistent writes.
Existing new-format values are not silently replaced. Storage failure keeps
the session playable in memory and shows that persistence is unavailable.
Erasing scores affects new arcade keys only and requires a second explicit
confirmation. Death counts and original standalone saves are not erased.

The desktop app reuses the old Scribble Defender profile directory, avoiding
a forced Chromium profile reset. Browsers still enforce origin/profile
boundaries, especially file URLs. The shell cannot read another browser,
profile or isolated file origin. Import/export is provided for that case.
Rollback is opening the old release: its original files and save keys remain.

Titles closest to their inspirations are centralized in src/catalog.js.
Changing Snack-Man, Q*Nerd or Dunce Kong never changes save IDs. No new
characters or game likenesses are introduced in Phase 1. Future game rules,
research, intentional differences and session tests belong to their phases.

## v0.4.0 input and progression revision

Seven game notebook positions plus one replay sketchbook keep physical notebooks at eight. Only ready games can unlock. Progression is configured centrally, starting Defender, Erasteroids, Space Substitutes, Detention Breakout, Spitball Command, Quiz, Snack-Man. Default target is the previous notebook best of 10,000 points. The optional override unlocks ready builds only, never unfinished games. First-launch comic state uses No2Arcade:intro:seen. Hold-based skipping requires an uninterrupted 0.8 seconds; release resets the meter. DevicePrompts polls controller connection and emits Xbox labels. Comic playback is UI time, independent of the preserved 120 Hz game simulation.


## v0.4.1 correction and physical presentation contract

This section supersedes the historical v0.4.0 progression revision above.
All 24 notebooks are visible and openable. All notebooks unlocked defaults
ON; progression is opt-in and never hides unbuilt page scaffolds. A one-time
migration corrects v0.4.0 defaults without rewriting legacy Defender saves.
Six portrait game books plus a distinct replay sketchbook occupy the desk.
The backpack is one readable 24-cover grid with pin/unpin and replacement.

Centimeters define every physical object's bounds. Hub camera height is
90 cm, open-book and replay camera height 34 cm, with one uniform scale and
a 600 ms eased move. A selected notebook moves to the central workspace.
The desk plane extends beyond ultrawide views. Props do not independently
resize. DOM uses 12 design pixels per cm before the same camera transform.
The game samples the registered paper crop underneath its viewport, while
keeping the original DOM-independent 120 Hz simulation and draw-list source.
Presentation adapters own opaque text tags, minimum sizes and page-edge tabs.

The intro owns UI-time guided panels, outgoing-page turns, reduced-motion
crossfades, hold-to-skip and final camera handoff. It never steps the game.
Comic budget is 32 MiB logical source pixels, normally no more than two
12 MiB portraits during a turn. Hub budget is 32 MiB, game-atlas budget is
96 MiB per notebook, and total single-file HTML budget is 64 MiB. Source-pixel
budgets exclude mipmaps, framebuffer allocations, decoding copies and driver
caches. AssetService owns ImageSource resources, releases non-hub textures on
close and never relies on shared Pixi global-cache destruction.

The contract fields remain id, title, version, paper/cover IDs, seeded init,
fixed-step update, draw list, input/rebinding, scoring/table ID, cheat sheet,
per-game settings, attract and deterministic tests. No new gameplay deviation
for Defender. All historical engine notes and checks remain applicable.

All dimensions below are delivered 2x source pixels. Each current asset is one frame at 0 fps, pivot (0.5, 0.5). Original raster masters are retained in authored/. Swapping an image while retaining its filename, dimensions, alpha, pivot and manifest ID needs no code changes. The file manifest is validated at build and in QA.

Physical hero elements are authored images, not canvas path illustrations. The manufactured ruling on paper is composed over an authored paper crop. Variations of one notebook family are explicitly derived colour treatments, not falsely described as separate photo shoots. The 23 blank books are page scaffolds, not placeholder gameplay sprites.

## Lighting, ink and ownership

Warm key from upper left is authored into new physical objects. Alpha includes soft contact shadow. These are AI-generated photographed-style materials, not actual photography, scans or measured PBR maps. New pages and ink use transparent source assets with multiply compositing. The unchanged Defender package retains all of its existing normal/roughness/ink/post pipeline. Do not overwrite that package while adding future games.

Hub thumbnails are lightweight shared UI art. Full covers/papers load when their notebook opens. Defender game atlases live only in its own compressed module pack and are destroyed on close. See MODULE_CONTRACT.md for explicit pixel budgets and limits.

## Intro comic

Nine original authored comic pages: eight 1536x2048 portraits and one 2048x1365 arcade spread. One frame per asset, center pivot. Retained original generation masters and a curated original arcade spread supply the ink. Two guided panels per portrait and three stops across the spread; whole-page beats, eased travel, caption and balloon reveals and restrained detail motion. Current page decodes on demand; outgoing page releases after its shaded corner turn. Logical source-pixel budget 32 MiB, normally at most 24 MiB for two portrait pages. A dedicated 21x28 cm elastic-bound sketchbook replays the intro. Automatic sequence is about 79 seconds plus handoff. Tap advances a panel. Hold A/Space or the physical skip control continuously for 0.8 seconds to skip. Reduced motion highlights panels and crossfades without curls. No copied cabinets, art, recordings or logos.

Add the game module, its pack manifest and source art, keeping stable IDs and registered dimensions. Pack gameplay atlases per notebook. # Scribble Defender v0.3.2  -  asset contract

Status: v0.3.2 contains integrated authored images. Ten original AI-generated raster masters are retained under authored/ with provenance. No placeholder images remain. Detail components baked into a base image use neutral auxiliary overlays to prevent doubling. Normal/roughness support is derived, not physically measured.

## Drop-in workflow

Replace files at the exact paths below. Preserve RGBA, dimensions, frame registration, pivot, map conventions, row-major frame order. Change `placeholder` to false only after visual review; record author/license in LICENSES.md. Run `node pipeline.cjs`; no gameplay or renderer edits. Frame dimensions are at **2x**; sheet columns = min(frame count, floor(8192 / frame width)), sheet rows = ceil(frame count / columns); static files have one column. Frame count 1/FPS 0 is static. Pivots are normalized to each frame. Runtime atlases downsample source art to 1x on the balanced profile; original source files retain full 2x resolution. Never put text into reserved UI writing zones.

## Production rules

Photograph/scan at 600 dpi in diffuse light with color chart. Derive normal/roughness from capture or sculpted height, never luminance-only inference of a final albedo. Albedo contains no key light; renderer supplies warm top-left lighting. Shadow masks use alpha (white RGB); transparent outside. Straight alpha exports, 4 px atlas padding, no trimming/rotation. Ink multiply, highlighter additive, white-out normal; Sharpie bleed authored in texture. Carvings are hand cuts/sculpted grooves, never fonts. Desk crop uses cover, every prop/page uses uniform scale. Paper variants must not include recurring text.

Hero art is raster-only in the runtime. Placeholder generation uses simple raster silhouettes/labels to expose missing art, not procedural imitation of final assets. No legacy vector hero renderer is loaded.

## Memory / performance

Atlas maximum 2048², tightly packed with 4px extrusion; no mipmaps in balanced profile. Sum decoded RGBA atlas bytes must be <128 MiB; pipeline fails otherwise. Desk and material maps are independent textures. Lit materials share one static world-space normal/roughness pass, cached until resize; unlit ink stays outside it. Post grain/vignette/depth-of-field are independently toggleable. Integrated/discrete frame targets require device measurements, never inferred from headless throughput.

## Icon source

icons/ and player-idle use the same placeholder raster master until the scanned player exists. Tier-specific pixel simplification is required. 16/24 edges are snapped individually. ICO: 16,20,24,32,40,48,64,96,128 BMP32+alpha and 256 PNG; favicon 16/32/48. Apple 180; app 192/512; maskable central 80%. Windows file association controls the HTML file icon. Local file installation is browser-dependent; a data manifest alone cannot promise PWA install on file://.
